ココ.role: the heroine; a wounded demi-human girl the protagonist takes in and lives with
ココ.register: polite です/ます, heavy stutter and trailing ellipses at first, warmer and franker as affection rises

ネロ.role: default name of the player character, a lone scavenger; the player may rename him, so the name arrives through a variable

セレナ.role: black-market trader; buys scrap, hands out material fetch-quests, sexually forward and teasing
セレナ.register: casual, drawn-out playful vowels (呼んだ～?), pushy

ガノーザ.role: Koko's mother; a mature demi-human, meek and easily flustered
ガノーザ.register: timid, apologetic, whimpering fillers (ふぇえぇ)

ネモ.role: the second black-market trader, alongside Serena

島守匠海.role: easter-egg name the player can enter; grants a survival-skill bonus

佐藤久雄.role: easter-egg name the player can enter

ガスター.role: easter-egg name; entering it closes the game

ママ.role: Ganoza referred to as mother in dialogue

notes: The protagonist's name reaches dialogue through a variable, so it arrives as a sentinel. Never write 'Nero' into a line that has a sentinel standing for his name.
Trust the dialogue over the name when deciding gender. Ganoza and Serena are both women despite the unfamiliar readings.
Koko and Ganoza are daughter and mother. Ganoza is 'the mother' / 'Mom' in the three-way scenes, never a sister.

The five lewd-word arrays (f.ingo_tinko / _jyoseiki / _anal / _samen / _zettyou) are a five-rung ladder from coy to degrading. Translate them as a set, not line by line, and keep each entry short enough to splice mid-sentence.
'同棲' + a number + '日目' is assembled at run time into the day counter. Render the pair so the whole thing reads naturally in English, e.g. '同棲' -> 'Day ' and '日目' -> ' together'.
Honorific policy: drop -san/-chan in prose ('Ganoza-san' -> 'Ganoza'), but keep a bare 'Miss' only where the deference is the point. Do not romanise honorifics into the middle of English sentences.
